articles.title: Elon Musk's SpaceX just made a huge play to challenge the phone industry and stocks like AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon are getting crushed - Yahoo Finance
articles.summary: Elon Musk's SpaceX just made a huge play to challenge the phone industry and stocks like AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon are getting crushed  Yahoo FinanceSpaceX deal to acquire spectrum license hammers shares of AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile  CNBCIs T Mobile US (TMUS) Ready For A New Wireless Threat?  Yahoo FinanceSpaceX Announces Spectrum Deal for Starlink Mobile Phone Service  Bloomberg.comSpaceX takes aim at US wireless carriers with spectrum acquisiti...
articles.full_text:
Elon Musk's SpaceX (SPCX) just sent a big message to the wireless industry.
We want our piece of the subscriber pie.
Late Thursday, SpaceX said it will acquire a nationwide low-band spectrum portfolio. It positions Musk's satellite business Starlink to challenge legacy wireless giants across the US.
Shares of AT&T (T), T-Mobile (TMUS) and Verizon (VZ) were crushed in afterhours trading on the news.
Concerns had already escalated across Wall Street that Starlink could disrupt legacy wireless operators like AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile by transitioning from a rural broadband service into a direct mobile competitor.
Following its strategic acquisition of terrestrial spectrum and rapid deployment of advanced satellites, SpaceX had laid the groundwork to launch its own standalone cellular network alongside its direct-to-cell capabilities.
The expansion threatens traditional carriers' high-margin enterprise, emergency service, and rural subscriber bases, as well as lucrative international roaming revenues.
AT&T CEO John Stankey has taken notice of Starlink's moves, but hasn't lost sleep over it…yet.
"I think they're going to find places where they clearly have a good solution," Stankey told Yahoo Finance at the Goldman Sachs Communacopia conference in September. "In airlines and flights today, they have a fantastic broadband solution. In rural parts or territories, it's a very efficient way to get good bandwidth to people. I think we see that there's going to be some IoT-type applications, like connecting vehicles that are largely outdoors and maybe have line of sight to the sky, that they're going to have an opportunity to go in and do some things there that maybe we haven't done as effectively."
So, while Starlink will present competition, Stankey added, "there's also going to be the complementary dynamic of us being able to solve that other 2% of the use cases I talked about and bring our customers to those satellite operators, whether it be Amazon or SpaceX. They'll be the beneficiary of us aggregating that traffic and bringing it into the wholesale market to be able to be used."

articles.title: Iranian protester hanged hours after marrying his imprisoned fiancée over jail phone line - Fox News
articles.summary: Iranian protester hanged hours after marrying his imprisoned fiancée over jail phone line  Fox NewsSpared, married, hanged: the last weeks of Iranian protester Alireza Sepahi  YahooTill death us do part: Iran’s prisoners marry before the gallows  The TimesIran protester recounts torture, mock execution after January arrest  Iran InternationalIranian January Protester Sentenced to Death in Shirvan Following Torture  IranWire
articles.full_text:
An Iranian anti-regime protester was hanged at dawn Oct. 5 inside Isfahan Central Prison, just hours after marrying his imprisoned fiancée over a jail phone line, The Times reported Thursday.
Alireza Sepahi, 25, was executed alongside co-defendant Alireza Raisi after being sentenced to death in the anti-government demonstrations at Isfahan’s Alikhani Square Jan. 8., according to Human Rights Iran.
Sepahi and his bride, student activist Mahshad Keshani, 22, knew and loved each other before being arrested during anti-regime demonstrations, the report said.
Keshani, who is serving a five-year sentence, pushed for an informal wedding Sunday as fears mounted that Sepahi’s execution was imminent after a final family summons.
The couple exchanged vows over the phone from inside Isfahan prison, joined by their fathers.
Human rights lawyer Amirsalar Davoudi facilitated the ceremony by reading the vows for the fathers to bless.
Keshani’s family gave a copy of the Quran, a saffron rock candy and a single red rose as a traditional dowry.
"It was Mahshad’s idea," Davoudi told The Times. "Even now, I wonder how one young woman can possess such courage."
Davoudi recalled warning Keshani about the permanent nature of the decision.
"I told her, ‘My dear, you understand that this cannot simply be undone?’" Davoudi said.
"She said, ‘Mr Davoudi, I love Alireza.’"
When Davoudi presented the proposal to Sepahi, the young man broke down in tears.
"Alireza was crying, and something deeply painful and beautiful happened. Even the prison officers began to cry," Davoudi said.
The ceremony held no formal authority to halt the execution. Sepahi had previously survived a scheduled hanging in July after suffering a heart attack on his way to the gallows. Authorities then rescheduled the execution after he regained consciousness.
On Monday morning, hours after the vows were spoken, Sepahi was hanged.
He is among seven defendants executed in the Alikhani Square case, in which 12 men were accused in the deaths of four security personnel.
After the hanging, Sepahi’s family was reportedly prevented by authorities from burying their son in his hometown.
Davoudi condemned the Iranian regime's actions.
"I do not know how to come to terms with this," Davoudi said.
"The regime is taking revenge on innocent young people for the humiliation it has suffered internationally."
Human rights groups report Keshani remains in custody, facing additional security charges.
This came as Maryam Rajavi, president-elect of the National Council of Resistance of Iran (NCRI), urged U.N. Secretary-General António Guterres to take immediate international action to halt executions and the killing of protesters in Iran, citing thousands of executions and decades of impunity for human rights abuses.
In a letter ahead of World Day Against the Death Penalty on Oct. 10, Rajavi called for international accountability, independent investigations and diplomatic and economic pressure on Tehran to end the executions.

articles.title: UAE, Thailand conclude trade deal talks after non-oil trade jumps 75% - Gulf News
articles.summary: UAE, Thailand conclude trade deal talks after non-oil trade jumps 75%  Gulf News
articles.full_text:
Bilateral non-oil trade reached $10.2 billion in the first half of 2026
The conclusion of negotiations was announced in Bangkok during a meeting between Dr. Thani bin Ahmed Al Zeyoudi, UAE Minister of Foreign Trade; Anutin Charnvirakul, Prime Minister of the Kingdom of Thailand; and Suphajee Suthumpun, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Commerce of the Kingdom of Thailand, in the presence of Obaid Saeed Al Dhaheri, UAE Ambassador to the Kingdom of Thailand.
The agreement is expected to strengthen trade and investment ties between the two economies, with the two sides looking to expand cooperation between their business communities.
Bilateral non-oil trade reached $12.3 billion in 2025, an increase of 65.2 per cent from the previous year, according to the UAE government.
Trade continued to grow in the first half of 2026, reaching $10.2 billion, up 75.4 per cent from the same period in 2025.
UAE non-oil exports to Thailand reached US$4.5 billion in 2025, driven by growth in gold, aluminium products and other industrial goods, while imports from Thailand reached US$7.2 billion.
Dr Thani bin Ahmed Al Zeyoudi, UAE Minister of Foreign Trade, said the conclusion of negotiations reflected the two countries’ commitment to strengthening economic ties between Southeast Asia and the Middle East.
“The conclusion of negotiations on the UAE-Thailand CEPA embodies our shared commitment to building stronger economic bridges between Southeast Asia and the Middle East,” Al Zeyoudi said.
“Thailand is one of the most dynamic and diversified economies in the region, and this agreement will open new avenues for companies, investors and entrepreneurs in both countries to expand and access high-growth markets,” he added.
Al Zeyoudi said the agreement would reduce trade barriers, enhance market access and support investment flows.
“By reducing trade barriers, enhancing market access and stimulating investment flows, the CEPA will support our long-term economic objectives and generate new opportunities across a wide range of strategic sectors,” he said.
He added that the agreement would reinforce the UAE’s position as a global hub for trade and investment connecting markets across Asia, Africa and Europe.
Meanwhile, Anutin Charnvirakul, Prime Minister of the Kingdom of Thailand, said the agreement would take economic and trade relations between Thailand and the UAE to a new level.
He said the conclusion of negotiations demonstrated both countries’ commitment to expanding cooperation and creating mutual benefits.
The agreement is expected to create opportunities for private-sector companies and business communities in both countries, strengthen two-way investment and support economic growth, while improving the competitiveness of Emirati and Thai companies in each other’s markets and across the wider region.
Once signed, ratified and brought into force, the CEPA is expected to support trade and investment in sectors including advanced manufacturing, logistics, food security, digital trade, renewable energy and precious metals.
During his visit, Al Zeyoudi also held meetings with Thai companies and institutions operating across the trade, investment, industrial and services sectors.
Discussions focused on expanding partnerships and two-way investment, developing supply chains and increasing trade and investment flows between the two markets.
Negotiations on the UAE-Thailand CEPA began in May 2023, following the establishment of the first UAE-Thai Business Council in February that year.
The two countries will now complete the legal and technical procedures required for the agreement to be formally signed and enter into force.
The UAE government said the CEPA is expected to create a more stable and attractive business environment while opening further opportunities for companies and consumers in both countries.

articles.summary: Nano One Secures Global LFP Feedstock Supply Chain Ahead of 2027  ChemAnalyst
articles.full_text:
Welcome To ChemAnalyst
	Nano One Materials Corp. has reached a major milestone in its lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cathode production strategy, advancing the qualification of raw-material suppliers across North America, Europe and South America as it prepares to expand production outside Asia.
	The company said a diversified group of lithium carbonate and phosphoric acid suppliers has now been pre-qualified for LFP cathode production, while multiple iron oxide sources are progressing through validation. Feedstock sources have been identified across Canada, the United States, Europe, Chile and Argentina, supporting Nano One’s planned Canada Development Company (DevCo) project and broader commercialisation strategy.
	Three lithium carbonate suppliers from Argentina and Chile have completed pre-qualification, while two additional suppliers from Canada and the United States remain under assessment. On the phosphate side, three phosphoric acid suppliers from the United States and Europe have been pre-qualified, with two Canadian development-stage sources beginning sampling.
	Iron remains a key focus. A Canadian iron oxide supplier is progressing toward tonne-scale validation, while a European source is also undergoing validation. Five additional iron suppliers are currently under development.
	Nano One’s qualification process tests feedstocks at pilot-reactor scale to assess cathode material quality and consistency. The company noted that conventional qualification can take up to two years as materials progress from gram-to-kilogram A-Samples through larger B- and C-Sample stages. By completing this work early, future projects using its technology could potentially move toward production more quickly.
	The company’s patented One-Pot process is central to the strategy. Unlike conventional LFP manufacturing, which often relies on externally produced iron phosphate precursor (pCAM), One-Pot directly combines lithium carbonate, iron and phosphoric acid to produce LFP cathode material.
	This approach could help manufacturers outside China reduce exposure to concentrated precursor supply chains. Nano One highlighted that China accounts for more than 95% of precursor cathode material production, making feedstock diversification increasingly important for companies seeking secure regional supply chains.
	The development also strengthens Nano One’s licensing proposition. Future licensees could potentially access established feedstock specifications and pre-qualified suppliers rather than beginning qualification programs from scratch, potentially shortening project development timelines.
	Demand from energy storage remains a major driver for LFP, while defence applications are emerging as a strategically important market because of increasingly stringent sourcing requirements. Nano One said its Canadian supply-chain strategy aligns with growing requirements for secure and non-foreign-entity-of-concern (FEOC) battery materials.
	The company continues to target initial commercial LFP supply agreements for smaller-scale defence and energy-storage applications. Its expanded Candiac facility, with approximately 800 tonnes per year of planned capacity, is expected to be commissioned in the first half of 2027.
	Product and Chemical Commodity Price Impact
Nano One’s progress could strengthen the commercial outlook for LFP cathode active materials, lithium carbonate and phosphoric acid, while improving supply-chain resilience outside Asia. Pre-qualified suppliers across Chile, Argentina, Canada, the United States and Europe may reduce procurement risks and provide future LFP producers with alternative feedstock sources. In the near term, the announcement is unlikely to trigger a major price movement because it represents qualification and development rather than a large immediate increase in consumption. However, successful commercialisation could support lithium carbonate demand and potentially tighten regional supply balances. Greater use of diversified iron and phosphate sources may also reduce dependency-driven premiums for LFP-related materials over time.

articles.full_text:
The UAE and Thailand have concluded negotiations on their Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement, a deal expected to lower trade barriers and strengthen bilateral relations, according to The National.
The two countries started talks on the agreement in 2023 and set up a joint business council that same year, the Ministry of Foreign Trade said in a statement on Thursday.
During the negotiations, the sides examined ways to increase trade and investment and to widen co-operation, the ministry said. In the next stage, the UAE and Thailand will complete the legal and technical steps needed for the agreement to be signed and brought into effect.
The agreement is expected to speed up trade flows, open new investment opportunities and deepen private sector co-operation in priority areas such as advanced manufacturing, logistics, food security, digital trade, renewable energy and precious metals.
Minister of Foreign Trade Dr Thani Al Zeyoudi said the conclusion of negotiations reflected a shared commitment to building stronger economic bridges between South-East Asia and the Middle East. He described Thailand as one of the most dynamic and diversified economies in the region and said the agreement would create new avenues for companies, investors and entrepreneurs in both countries to expand and reach high-growth markets.
The deal builds on established ties between the UAE and Thailand. Bilateral non-oil trade in the first half of 2026 rose by more than 75 per cent year-on-year to $10.2 billion, while trade last year grew by more than 65 per cent to $12.3 billion.
The UAE's main non-oil exports to Thailand include gold, aluminium and other industrial goods.
The ministry said the figures pointed to growing integration between the two economies and to the scale of opportunity the agreement could unlock. Dr Al Zeyoudi added that by reducing trade barriers, improving market access and stimulating investment flows, the agreement would support long-term economic objectives and generate new opportunities across a wide range of strategic sectors.
The UAE has signed 38 Cepas with trading partners as it seeks to boost investment ties, expand its non-oil economic base and broaden exports. The Cepa programme is a key pillar of the UAE's foreign trade agenda, which aims to raise non-oil foreign trade to Dh4 trillion, or $1.1 trillion, by 2031.

articles.title: Zeekr 007 GT set for Q4 Australian launch after roll-out in 16 European countries - CnEVPost
articles.summary: Zeekr 007 GT set for Q4 Australian launch after roll-out in 16 European countries  CnEVPost
articles.full_text:
- The electric shooting brake made its public appearance at the Sydney EV show and will enter Australia as the Zeekr 7GT.
- The 007 GT is already available in 16 European countries, with the planned Australian launch set to expand its overseas footprint.
Zeekr, the premium brand of Geely Auto (HKEX: 0175), plans to officially launch its 007 GT electric shooting brake in Australia in the fourth quarter of 2026, further expanding the model's overseas presence.
Zeekr announced the plan on its official Weibo account on Thursday, saying the 007 GT had made its first public appearance at the Sydney EV show in Australia. The model is known as the Zeekr 7GT in overseas markets.
The announcement did not disclose pricing, detailed specifications or delivery timing for the Australian version. The planned launch follows the model's expansion in Europe this year.
The Zeekr 007 GT was launched in Germany, the Netherlands, Belgium, Denmark, Norway and Sweden in January. By July, its European presence had expanded to 16 countries, including France, Italy and Spain.
The model was first launched in China in April 2025. Based on the Zeekr 007 electric sedan, it is the brand's second shooting brake after the 001.
Zeekr launched updated versions of the 007 and 007 GT in China in April this year, upgrading both to a 900-volt architecture with support for charging rates of up to 6C. The latest announcement did not specify whether these features would be offered on the Australian model.
Zeekr is drawing on its shooting brake sales performance to support its overseas expansion. Citing wholesale data from the China Passenger Car Association (CPCA), the company said the 007 GT ranked first in global shooting brake sales in the first 8 months of 2026.
The company also said global deliveries of its shooting brake models remained above 10,000 in August, with cumulative sales exceeding 400,000. The cumulative figure covers its shooting brake lineup, rather than the 007 GT alone.
The overseas push comes as Zeekr's overall deliveries continue to grow. The brand delivered 37,216 vehicles in September, up 103.85% year-on-year and setting a monthly record for the sixth consecutive month.
Zeekr delivered 288,404 vehicles in the first 9 months of this year, up 100.84% year-on-year, according to data previously reported by CnEVPost.

For Immediate Release
Chicago, IL – October 8, 2026 – Today, Zacks Equity as Similarweb SMWB and Perion Network PERI
Industry: Internet Content
Link: https://www.zacks.com/commentary/3002117/2-internet-content-stocks-to-buy-from-a-challenging-industry
The Zacks Internet - Content has been suffering from challenging macroeconomic conditions globally, which is causing a detrimental effect on advertising spending, the primary revenue source for industry participants. Rising AI infrastructure and hosting costs, as well as continuous pressure to improve monetization, have been concerns for industry players.
However, industry participants like Similarweb and Perion Network are expanding their presence across multiple channels, driving top-line growth. These companies are benefiting from solid demand for digital offerings, as well as the increasing importance of video content and cloud-based applications. The rapid deployment of AI, Generative AI and Large Language Models (LLMs) is aiding industry players in enhancing the recommendation and search functions of their platforms, thereby improving user experience.
Industry Description
The Zacks Internet - Content industry comprises providers of video encoding platforms, personal services, Internet content and information, staffing and outsourcing services, publishing, capital markets, media-based, home service, digital insights and measurement, stock photo, video and music licensing, and online travel companies.
The industry is witnessing a rapid change in consumer behavior and ongoing digitalization. Advertising is a major revenue source for industry participants. Therefore, these companies are trying to expand their digital presence to win customers. They are also expanding their presence across social media, display, connected TV and search. Apart from the United States, a number of companies in this industry are located in Israel, the U.K., Germany, Russia and China.
4 Trends Shaping the Future of the Internet - Content Industry
Demand for Digital Offerings Growing: The shift from traditional search to AI assistants, conversational interfaces, and agentic AI is reshaping how users discover content and interact online. The companies in the Zacks Internet Content industry are continually adapting their products, monetization strategies and distribution models to remain relevant as user behavior evolves and AI platforms become new gateways to digital content.
Industry Prospects Driven by Ad Spending Rate: Industry participants are focusing on marketing efforts to boost traffic to websites. Advertising and subscriptions are major revenue sources for these companies. The industry is dependent on consumer spending trends, making holiday spending a major deciding factor. However, macroeconomic challenges are expected to hurt ad spending.
Rising Competition for Users, Content and AI Leadership: The industry is facing intense competition for user engagement, premium content creators and enterprise customers. User engagement alone is no longer enough. Companies must consistently improve advertising ROI, increase customer retention, expand cross-selling and introduce new monetization models such as AI licensing and consumption-based pricing.
Increasing Regulations Mar Prospects: Industry participants involved in online search and other social networking activities are increasingly facing regulatory pressure, particularly in China and the European Union (EU). The China government has a number of regulations related to direct advertising, which is a prime revenue source for these companies.
The implementation of the General Data Protection Regulation in the EU adds to the concerns. Enactment of the Digital Markets Act (DMA) in the EU aims to prevent large online platforms that connect users with content, goods, information and services from abusing their market power. The DMA adds to the headwinds faced by Internet content providers in the EU.
Zacks Industry Rank Indicates Dim Prospects
The Zacks Internet - Content industry is housed within the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector. It carries a Zacks Industry Rank #233, which places it in the bottom 6% of more than 247 Zacks industries.
The group’s Zacks Industry Rank, which is the average of the Zacks Rank of all the member stocks, indicates dim near-term prospects. Our research shows that the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries outperform the bottom 50% by a factor of more than two to one.
The industry’s position in the bottom 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries is a result of a negative earnings outlook for the constituent companies in aggregate. Looking at the aggregate earnings estimate revisions, it appears that analysts are pessimistic about this group’s earnings growth potential. Since Jan. 31, 2026, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the industry’s 2026 earnings has moved down 17.2%.
Given the bearish industry outlook, there are only a few stocks worth buying. But before we present the stocks that you may want to consider for your portfolio, let us take a look at the industry’s recent stock market performance and valuation.
Industry Lags S&P and Sector
The Zacks Internet - Content industry has underperformed the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector, as well as the S&P 500 composite, over the past year.
The industry has declined 29.1% over this period compared with the S&P 500’s appreciation of 16.8% and the 28.7% increase of the broader sector.
Industry's Current Valuation
On the basis of the trailing 12-month price-to-sales ratio (P/S), which is a commonly used multiple for valuing Internet – Content stocks, we see that the industry is currently trading at 5.70X compared with the S&P 500’s 5.93X and the sector’s 8.88X.
Over the last five years, the industry has traded as high as 7.80X and as low as 4.72X, the median being 5.87X.
2 Internet Stocks to Buy
Similarweb: This Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) company is benefiting from growing demand for its proprietary digital data from AI companies and large enterprises. You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.
AI-related revenues reached 13% of total revenues in the second quarter of 2026, up from 11% at the end of 2025. The company signed three large multi-year enterprise contracts with a cumulative value of more than $60 million, including a deal with a leading technology company using Similarweb data for Large Language Model (LLM) training. Growing demand for Similarweb’s data across AI agents, OEMs and other enterprise AI applications is creating opportunities to increase data consumption and expand average deal sizes. Remaining Performance Obligation increased 26% year over year to $345 million at the end of second-quarter 2026.
The Zacks Consensus Estimate for SMWB’s 2026 earnings has been steady at 22 cents per share over the past 30 days. Similarweb shares have increased 7.2% on a year-to-date basis.
Perion Network: This Zacks Rank #2 company is benefiting from accelerating adoption of Perion One as advertisers shift budgets toward CTV, Digital Out of Home and Retail Media. Perion One spend increased 15% year over year to $156.7 million in the second quarter of 2026 and represented 80% of total spend. Outmax, Perion’s AI-powered optimization agent, also recorded 136% year-over-year pro-forma spend growth, supporting the company’s land-and-expand strategy across advertisers and agencies.
Perion’s recently signed large-scale strategic agreements provide a catalyst for stronger growth in the second half of 2026 and into 2027. The company expects these deals to begin making a material contribution toward the end of the third quarter and accelerate thereafter.
The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Perion’s 2026 earnings has been steady at $1.17 per share over the past 30 days. PERI shares have dropped 10.8% YTD.

articles.title: Huawei’s Eric Xu: China May Come to Share U.S. AI Risk Concerns as Its Technology Advances - Pekingnology
articles.summary: Huawei’s Eric Xu: China May Come to Share U.S. AI Risk Concerns as Its Technology Advances  Pekingnology
articles.full_text:
Huawei’s rotating chairman Eric Zhijun Xu at Huawei Connect 2026 in mid-September sat down with journalists alongside Liao Heng, Huawei’s chief scientist for semiconductors, for an extensive discussion of the company’s AI computing strategy. Multiple Chinese media outlets, including Guancha, published the same transcript on Tuesday, Oct. 6.
Much of the conversation was highly technical, covering Huawei’s new computing architecture, chip interconnection technologies, and its efforts to compete with Nvidia despite restrictions on access to advanced semiconductor manufacturing.
But five remarks stand out for a broader audience, without having to delve into the technological details.
1. China may eventually share American companies’ concerns about AI risks—but for now, it needs to accelerate.
Asked about calls by some leading American AI developers to slow down AI development, Xu offered an interesting explanation for why Chinese companies may see the risks differently. American frontier developers possess considerably greater computing resources and may have reached levels of AI capability that Chinese developers have yet to experience.
“Several leading American model developers have access to much greater computing power. Exactly how far they have progressed is something that perhaps only they themselves know. The AI risks they are experiencing may not yet be felt nearly as strongly in China.
For now, China still needs to accelerate its own pace of development. Once we reach the point where we can genuinely perceive those risks, perhaps we will feel the same way as the leading American model developers. But I have always believed that we must both advance AI development and manage its risks. We must ensure that AI is used for good rather than for evil.”
Xu’s point is not that those risks are imaginary or should be disregarded. Rather, he suggests that China may come to share American frontier developers’ concerns as its own AI capabilities advance.
2. The global AI hardware supply crunch may not end until 2029—and China could take longer.
The rapid expansion of AI infrastructure has strained global supplies of chips, memory, optical networking equipment, and other critical components. Xu believes the industry was not prepared for the speed of growth and predicts that supply will take several more years to catch up with demand.
“The reason optical module manufacturers and memory companies can charge such high prices today is not that their products are necessarily exceptionally good. It is because demand vastly exceeds supply.
Therefore, these bottlenecks will not be fully resolved until supply and demand reach equilibrium both globally and in China. I expect the global supply-demand imbalance to be largely resolved around 2029. China may take a little longer.”
His forecast is particularly notable given China’s additional constraints on access to advanced semiconductor technologies. It also suggests that the current boom in AI infrastructure investment may continue to face supply bottlenecks for several years.
3. Nvidia’s CUDA software advantage is becoming less formidable, according to Huawei’s semiconductor chief scientist.
Nvidia’s competitive strength extends well beyond its chips. Its CUDA software ecosystem has long made it difficult for AI developers to switch to alternative hardware, including Huawei’s Ascend processors.
But Liao Heng argues that advances in AI programming are beginning to erode this advantage.
“Today, with the emergence of new compiler languages, these tools are gradually replacing aspects of the CUDA-based development approach and weakening CUDA’s ecosystem barriers. Frontier laboratories no longer attach the same importance to CUDA that they did two years ago.
This represents the gradual dismantling of barriers at the software level. I believe we are approaching, or may even have reached, a point of balance. The gap has narrowed substantially.”
Liao also said that the overall gap between Nvidia and Ascend had narrowed considerably, including in how familiar developers find the programming environment. This is Huawei’s assessment rather than an independently established parity between the two ecosystems, but it addresses what has historically been one of Nvidia’s most important competitive advantages.
4. Huawei believes Ascend may already have overtaken Nvidia in China, but cannot meet domestic demand.
U.S. export restrictions have created opportunities for Chinese AI chipmakers, particularly Huawei. Xu made a striking claim about Ascend’s position in China, while acknowledging that the company’s manufacturing capacity remains insufficient.
“At present, our Ascend supply is still far from sufficient to meet domestic demand, so we have no plans for a comprehensive expansion into overseas markets.
There are indeed a small number of countries with particularly strong needs, and we have conducted tests and supplied products to them, but the quantities have been very small.
It is difficult to calculate Nvidia’s market share in China. However, based on the data we are able to gather, Ascend should already have surpassed Nvidia.”
Xu did not specify whether his comparison was based on shipments, revenue, computing capacity, or another measure, so the market-share claim cannot be independently assessed from his remarks alone. Nevertheless, it is noteworthy that Huawei now believes Ascend has surpassed Nvidia in its home market.
5. Huawei will prioritize Chinese customers, while serving a limited number of overseas buyers seeking alternatives.
Asked about reports that Malaysia was considering deploying sovereign AI infrastructure based on Huawei’s Ascend 910C, Xu acknowledged that geopolitical considerations and the desire to diversify suppliers could make Huawei attractive to some overseas customers.
But he made clear where the company’s priorities lie.
“As for balancing domestic and overseas demand, our principle is very straightforward. Our primary focus is the domestic market. We give priority to Chinese customers who urgently need computing power.
Overseas, we serve a small number of customers who cannot purchase alternative solutions, or who are determined to have another option.”
In other words, Huawei is not currently positioning Ascend for a broad international sales push. Instead, its limited overseas supplies are aimed primarily at customers who cannot obtain competing products or who want an alternative supplier, while China’s enormous domestic demand takes precedence.
The complete Q&A covers Huawei’s broader technological strategy, including its new Peerium computing architecture, UnifiedBus interconnection technology, plans for future Ascend chips, and efforts to improve the efficiency of large-scale AI training. It is very long and technical, so I will not put out a translation.
One other Huawei development during China’s just-concluded National Day holiday deserves attention. On October 5, Huawei and Qualcomm announced a multiyear patent cross-licensing agreement covering 5G, computing, AI, and networking, alongside Qualcomm’s planned purchase of certain Huawei patents in the United States.
Some Chinese media reports claimed that Qualcomm would become a net payer to Huawei under the licensing agreement—meaning it would pay Huawei more in royalties than it receives. Qualcomm subsequently disputed this, saying the terms were confidential and the reports incorrect.
Just over a month earlier, on August 26, Huawei and HP had announced a global patent cross-licensing agreement covering Wi-Fi technology, although HP subsequently emphasized that the deal settled a patent dispute rather than represented a broader strategic or commercial partnership.
There is something striking about a Chinese company subjected to years of U.S. sanctions continuing to conclude patent deals with some of America’s leading technology companies. Whatever the financial terms, these agreements offer tangible commercial recognition of the value of Huawei’s intellectual property.
They also present an interesting contrast with the ongoing federal criminal trial in Brooklyn, where U.S. prosecutors have accused Huawei of stealing American technology to build its telecommunications empire—allegations Huawei denies. The patent agreements offer a rather different perspective on Huawei’s technological capabilities.
Xu's framing on risk is candid in a way worth taking seriously. If concern about AI danger only shows up once a lab can feel it firsthand, the compute gap may also push back the point where Chinese developers treat safety as their own problem. That timing could matter a lot for anyone hoping for a US-China floor on dangerous capabilities. It also sits awkwardly next to his 2029 estimate for the hardware crunch, since a few more years of accelerating first is a long window. Thanks for translating the full transcript, the Guancha version would have been easy to miss outside Chinese-language circles.
The rule published on 15 January 2026 makes case-by-case review available below two numbers: total processing performance under 21,000 and total DRAM bandwidth under 6,500 GB/s. Both have to be met, not one of them. BIS names the H200 as an example of hardware falling below them, together with its equivalents and less advanced chips.
One side of that comparison is counted downstream of a licence decision rather than a purchase decision. Ascend's constraint, in his account, is supply against domestic demand. What reaches the other side goes through that route, case by case.

articles.summary: Why Is Huawei Promoting HarmonyOS for Global Expansion at This Moment?  36 Kr
articles.full_text:
Why is Huawei pushing HarmonyOS to go global at this moment?
Huawei Devices is venturing into overseas markets again with a brand-new approach.
On October 6, Huawei's official overseas account released an interview transcript. Yu Chengdong (Richard Yu), Executive Director of Huawei and Chairman of Huawei Devices BG, talked to international media about Huawei's latest progress in chips, HarmonyOS, AI, foldable screens and overseas markets.
He stated that the long-term strategy of Huawei's Devices business in the next decade will center on five major scenarios: Harmony Intelligent Mobility, Harmony Office, Smart Home, Sports & Health, and Audio-Visual Entertainment, to deliver a seamless AI life experience for all consumers.
Among all the updates, two points stand out: first, Huawei is considering gradually rolling out the HarmonyOS operating system to the global market, but this is only an initial plan that will be advanced step by step; second, the price of storage components has risen sharply, pushing up the cost of each mobile phone by more than 200 US dollars. Huawei has been trying to absorb the extra cost on its own, but its overall profit margin has dropped significantly, leaving the company no choice but to raise product prices in the future.
The fact that these two points were actively disclosed by the official itself sends a clear signal: Huawei's Devices business will take HarmonyOS as its core driver to expand into overseas markets on a large scale once again.
More importantly, Yu Chengdong made these remarks specifically for the overseas market audience.
Statistics show that HarmonyOS has already built a solid foundation.
Yu Chengdong revealed that at present, more than 90 million devices are running HarmonyOS 6 and HarmonyOS 7, covering smartphones, PCs and tablets. The figure is expected to reach 100 million by the end of 2026, marking that the HarmonyOS ecosystem has moved past the introduction phase and entered the growth phase.
In terms of the application ecosystem, the number of applications and services on HarmonyOS has exceeded 450,000, the number of registered global developers has reached 11 million, and the number of application innovation partners has surpassed 23,000.
In the first quarter of 2026, HarmonyOS overtook iOS for 7 consecutive quarters with a 19% market share, ranking second in China; its share rose to 24% in the second quarter, while iOS took 18% of the market. The Ministry of Industry and Information Technology of China also confirmed that HarmonyOS has become the world's third largest mobile operating system after Android and iOS, with a 5% global market share in the first quarter.
However, the ranking of second in China and third in the world does not mean that HarmonyOS is in a safe position. Yu Chengdong pointed out that the biggest challenges for operating systems lie in application development and ecosystem construction, which is the exact step where Microsoft's Windows Phone, Samsung's bada and Nokia's Symbian all failed completely.
At the moment, there are only two paths left for Huawei's Devices business to continue growing stronger: move up the value chain, or expand outward to overseas markets.
For the upward path, Huawei remains the only domestic Chinese brand that can compete head-to-head with Apple in the high-end market. Over the past 7 years, Huawei's mobile phone business has not only survived, but also captured almost all the domestic market share it could secure. In the second quarter of 2026, Huawei ranked first in China's smartphone market with a 23% share, while Apple ranked second with 18%.
This leaves only one viable path: to expand outward to overseas markets.
Selling mobile phones is a one-off transaction, while running an operating system is a recurring revenue business. Apple's App Store commission and Google's licensing fees are proven successful examples. If HarmonyOS is fully rolled out globally, Huawei's mobile phone business model will shift from selling hardware to the Apple-style integrated hardware and software model.
This is the most thorough strategic reassessment of Huawei's mobile phone business in the seven years since it was hit by supply restrictions.
Huawei has also prepared two new trump cards for this goal: an independent supply chain system and self-developed operating system. As Yu Chengdong put it, Huawei resumed localized supply of core mobile phone chips in 2023, and has basically got rid of its dependence on external technologies.
With all these conditions in place, HarmonyOS can officially put the "overseas expansion" plan on the table.
However, Yu Chengdong did not give a specific timetable for this new overseas expansion, and this public statement is more like a test of market response. Even so, the significance of HarmonyOS going global is far greater than the outside world expects.
Over the past two decades, Chinese technology companies' overseas expansion has gone through two phases. The first phase is product export, where hardware products are sold to all over the world; the second phase is model export, where platforms like TikTok and SHEIN replicate Chinese business models across the globe.
These two phases of overseas expansion share one common point: they are all built on underlying infrastructure owned by other parties. For example, Android, iOS and Windows, whose distribution rules, commission rates and review mechanisms are all set by others. The crisis Huawei faced in 2019 was exactly that its underlying support was taken away.
From my perspective, if HarmonyOS successfully goes global, it will very likely kick off the 3.0 phase of Chinese technology companies' overseas expansion: exporting the underlying digital infrastructure itself. Because operating systems are the "land" of the digital world, whoever owns an operating system is qualified to participate in the formulation of industry rules.
Huawei has accumulated sufficient resources for this goal for a very long time. On the one hand, it has achieved technological self-reliance: nearly half of Huawei's more than 200,000 employees are engaged in R&D, and the company's total R&D investment from 2007 to the end of 2025 exceeded 1.8 trillion yuan, with the R&D-to-revenue ratio rising from around 10% to over 20%.
The HarmonyOS ecosystem has also entered a positive cycle. HarmonyOS now has access to more than 400,000 applications and services, with over 100,000 native applications, a 97% adaptation rate for the top 100 mobile applications, and all high-frequency applications such as WeChat, Alipay, Douyin and Meituan are fully supported. Among them, the installed volume of the WeChat HarmonyOS version has exceeded 80 million.
On the other hand, Huawei has made efforts to adapt to international rules. On October 5, Huawei and Qualcomm just announced a multi-year patent cross-licensing agreement covering 5G, computing, AI, networking and other fields. Qualcomm will also acquire several of Huawei's US patents in the fields of computing, AI and networking, and the transaction is still pending regulatory approval.
This is the first 5G-covered cross-licensing agreement between the two parties, and it is the first time Qualcomm has paid patent royalties to Huawei. The total amount of Huawei's cumulative patent licensing agreements is expected to exceed 6.9 billion US dollars. The agreement repeatedly emphasizes the FRAND principle (Fair, Reasonable and Non-Discriminatory), which is equivalent to Huawei submitting a letter of commitment to comply with the international intellectual property rule system.
Among all Chinese technology companies, Huawei is currently the only one that can exchange standard essential patents with Qualcomm.
HarmonyOS Ecosystem Source: Screenshot from Huawei press conference
To a certain extent, HarmonyOS going global is equivalent to a corporate asset restructuring for Huawei. In the past, its Devices business followed the logic of the manufacturing industry, earning profit from each unit sold; now it shifts to the platform logic, where the sales volume of hardware such as mobile phones can be lower, but every HarmonyOS device acts as an access point to the ecosystem.
It can even be said that Huawei is currently following the successful path that Apple has taken. However, Yu Chengdong holds a very cautious attitude towards this overseas expansion. He said that Huawei's smartphone business has been severely affected since 2019: it once ranked first in the global market share, but now only sells several million units outside China every year.
This requires Huawei to rebuild its distribution channels, nurture the ecosystem, and refresh its brand recognition in overseas markets. The hardest part is trust building: operating systems hold users' data, payment channels and application distribution rights, so why would overseas users and developers hand over their digital lives to a Chinese operating system?
Fortunately, the foundation Huawei laid in the past is still solid. For example, its wearable devices rank first in market share both in China and across the globe, and its TWS earphones top the sales charts in many countries. Watches, earphones, tablets and vehicle infotainment systems rely far less on the application ecosystem than smartphones, and users who buy a Huawei watch do not care if it can install Instagram.
When expanding HarmonyOS to overseas markets, Huawei can temporarily put aside the mobile phone priority strategy, and first roll out a batch of devices that do not rely on Google's GMS suite, to gradually nurture the account system and developer ecosystem.
Emerging markets are another key entry point. Southeast Asia, the Middle East, Latin America and Africa are far less dependent on Google services than Europe and the United States, and their consumers are more price-sensitive. Users in these markets demand products that work well and are affordable, and do not insist on using Google services. Android captured these markets

articles.title: Commerce Minister says that a November signing of a US Thai trade deal is in sight as exporters stand by - Thai Examiner
articles.summary: Commerce Minister says that a November signing of a US Thai trade deal is in sight as exporters stand by  Thai Examiner
articles.full_text:
Trump wants a November trade deal with Thailand, but the final agreement remains unfinished. Anutin says talks are nearing completion as Suphajee targets the ASEAN summit. Meanwhile, American tariff threats persist and Vietnam moves ahead with talks.
A US–Thailand trade deal is heading for a November signing after President Donald Trump wrote directly to Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul. However, critical terms remain unresolved despite agreement in principle. Commerce Minister Suphajee Suthumpun is targeting the ASEAN summit in the Philippines. Meanwhile, Thai exporters face existing US tariffs and further Section 301 threats. Vietnam is advancing its own deal, while Thailand seeks parity with regional competitors. Even a November signing may leave exporters waiting for implementation.
Thailand and the United States are approaching a major reciprocal trade agreement, with formal signing now targeted for November. However, the final deal remains unfinished despite both governments reaching an agreement in principle.
US President Donald Trump has written directly to Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul, proposing a signing during his forthcoming Asian visit. Meanwhile, Deputy Prime Minister and Commerce Minister Suphajee Suthumpun confirmed Thursday that technical and legal negotiations were continuing.
The ASEAN summit in the Philippines has emerged as a possible venue. Nevertheless, Thai exporters still face uncertainty over American tariffs and the prospect of additional duties.
The latest developments follow three days of diplomatic exchanges between Bangkok and Washington. On Thursday, October 8, Suphajee met Anutin at Government House to review progress. Afterwards, she confirmed that both countries had settled the principal elements of the proposed agreement.
Thailand and US target November trade signing as Trump writes to Anutin but legal details remain
However, technical provisions, legal wording and other outstanding details still required attention. The Commerce Minister identified November as the anticipated signing period, particularly during the ASEAN summit in the Philippines. She stopped short of announcing a fixed date or confirming that the final document was ready.
The November timetable follows direct communication between Trump and Anutin. On Tuesday, October 6, government spokesman Ekkapop Pianpises confirmed that the American president had written to the Thai prime minister.
In his letter, Trump expressed interest in concluding negotiations and signing the agreement during his forthcoming Asian visit. Subsequently, Anutin instructed Suphajee to advance the remaining discussions and prepare the necessary arrangements.
The communication established a proposed political timetable for concluding the agreement. However, the final legal text remained unfinished, leaving further work for both negotiating teams.
Anutin says US trade deal is nearing completion as Suphajee confirms agreement on main principles
On Wednesday, October 7, Anutin addressed the negotiations during the Forbes Global CEO Conference in Singapore. Speaking before international business leaders, the prime minister described the agreement as approaching completion.
Indeed, he said both countries were effectively writing the final paragraph of their Agreement on Reciprocal Trade. He also disclosed Trump’s letter and its connection to the proposed signing. Nevertheless, Anutin did not announce that the agreement had been completed. His remarks indicated that the principal negotiating framework was settled, while the final legal provisions remained outstanding.
The following day, Suphajee provided a more detailed account of the remaining work. Following her meeting with Anutin, she confirmed that both countries had reached an agreement in principle.
However, technical and legal discussions were still underway. Importantly, she identified November as a possible signing window rather than a binding deadline. Her comments clarified the distinction between agreement on the main principles and completion of the final document. Consequently, the proposed November signing does not establish that negotiations have broken down or that Washington has rejected Thailand’s proposals.
ASEAN and APEC summits offer November signing opportunities while US tariff questions remain
Instead, both governments are continuing work on the outstanding provisions while preparing for a possible meeting between their leaders. The timing coincides with two major diplomatic gatherings in Asia.
The ASEAN summit is scheduled for November 16–18 in the Philippines. Subsequently, the APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting takes place in China on November 18–19. Both events have been mentioned as possible opportunities for Trump and Anutin to meet.
Nevertheless, no venue or signing date has been formally confirmed. Suphajee has specifically identified the ASEAN summit as a possible occasion for concluding the agreement.
Behind the diplomatic timetable, substantial commercial questions remain unresolved. In particular, the final American tariff treatment Thailand will secure remains a central question. The United States is Thailand’s largest export market, making the final terms important for manufacturers and exporters.
In September, Thai officials identified an existing 12.5% US tariff as a continuing concern. Moreover, they warned that a separate American investigation into industrial overcapacity could result in additional duties. That investigation remains distinct from the reciprocal trade discussions. Therefore, signing the bilateral agreement would not necessarily eliminate every potential American tariff measure.
Section 301 tariff threat remains as Thailand seeks US trade parity with Malaysia and Indonesia amid talks
The possibility of additional action under Section 301 of American trade law presents another unresolved issue. Such measures could impose further duties independently of the reciprocal agreement.
Meanwhile, Thailand is seeking trade conditions comparable to those available to regional competitors, particularly Malaysia and Indonesia. Both countries compete with Thailand in important manufacturing and export markets.
Accordingly, Bangkok has sought conditions that would prevent Thai exporters from facing less favourable American tariff treatment. However, the final tariff provisions have not been publicly confirmed, and negotiations over the remaining details are continuing.
Washington has also pressed Thailand on several issues beyond tariffs. These include market access, non-tariff barriers and investment conditions. Separately, purchases involving American agricultural commodities and aircraft have featured in the discussions.
The proposed agreement therefore covers a broader commercial relationship than the tariff rate alone. Nevertheless, the final provisions governing these matters remain outstanding. The two governments must settle the technical arrangements and legal wording before the document can be completed. Until then, the agreement in principle does not establish the precise commercial obligations that will apply.
November signing may precede Thai Cabinet, public hearings and parliamentary approval requirements
Furthermore, formal signing will not necessarily make the agreement immediately effective. Thai officials have previously identified domestic procedures that may be required before implementation.
These include Cabinet approval, public hearings and parliamentary consideration. Consequently, a November signing could be followed by additional legal and political steps in Thailand.
The timetable for implementation will depend on the completed text and the applicable approval requirements. Therefore, exporters face uncertainty over both the final tariff provisions and the date when any new arrangements would take effect.
For Thai businesses, the immediate position remains unchanged until the outstanding negotiations are concluded. The United States continues to represent Thailand’s largest export market. However, manufacturers still lack confirmation of the final reciprocal trade conditions.
Equally, the separate American investigation into industrial overcapacity remains a potential source of additional duties. Any further Section 301 action would create another trade issue outside the bilateral agreement. As a result, the proposed November signing cannot presently be treated as confirmation that all American tariff risks have been settled.
Vietnam advances US trade negotiations as Thailand seeks comparable terms with regional competitors
Meanwhile, developments elsewhere in Southeast Asia are adding urgency to the regional trade calendar. On Thursday, October 8, Vietnam announced that its reciprocal trade negotiations with Washington were largely completed.
The announcement followed seven rounds of discussions between the two countries. Vietnam’s progress came as Thailand confirmed its own agreement in principle. Nevertheless, neither announcement established that a completed agreement had entered into force.
Both countries maintain substantial manufacturing sectors and significant export relationships with the United States. Consequently, the final American trade conditions will be important for companies operating across regional supply chains.
Thailand’s negotiations also involve comparisons with Malaysia and Indonesia. Bangkok has sought tariff conditions comparable to those secured by these regional competitors. However, the precise treatment Thailand will receive remains subject to the final agreement.
The comparison is particularly relevant because manufacturers across Southeast Asia compete for orders in the American market. At the same time, Washington is negotiating trade arrangements with several regional economies. Therefore, the final terms agreed with Thailand will form part of a wider pattern of American trade conditions across Southeast Asia.

articles.full_text: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA or Agency) is approving a State Implementation Plan (SIP) revision submitted by the Commonwealth of Kentucky through the Energy and Environment Cabinet (Cabinet) on behalf of the Louisville Metro Air Pollution Control District (District) via a letter dated June 3, 2024. The SIP revision consists of a Limited Maintenance Plan (LMP) for the Kentucky portion of the bi-state Louisville, Kentucky-Indiana 1997 8-hour ozone maintenance area (the "bi-state Louisville Area"). The Kentucky portion of the bi-state Louisville Area is comprised of Bullitt, Jefferson, and Oldham Counties in Kentucky (the "Louisville Area"). The EPA is approving the Louisville Area's LMP because it provides for the maintenance of the 1997 8-hour ozone National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS) within the bi-state Louisville Area through the end of the second 10-year portion of the maintenance period. The effect of this action is to make certain commitments related to maintenance of the 1997 8-hour ozone NAAQS in the Louisville Area federally enforceable as part of the Kentucky SIP.

AGENCY:
Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service, USDA.
ACTION:
Final rule.
SUMMARY:
We are amending the regulations governing the importation of fresh cut flowers to remove requirements for the importation of specific types of cut flowers from the regulations, and to list them in the U.S. Department of Agriculture database called the Agricultural Commodity Import Requirements instead. We are also removing entirely any restrictions on the importation of fresh cut flowers of the genera
Chrysanthemum, Leucanthemella,
and
Nipponanthemum
from countries in which chrysanthemum white rust (
Puccinia horiana
P. Henn., CWR) is known to exist. This rule will allow us to use a notice-based, streamlined approach to update the import requirements for cut flowers and remove CWR-specific restrictions on the importation of fresh cut flowers.
DATES:
Effective November 9, 2026.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
Ms. Julie Orr, Regulatory Policy Specialist, Regulatory Coordination and Compliance, Pest Exclusion and Import Programs, APHIS, PPQ, 5601 Sunnyside Ave., Beltsville, MD 20705; (240) 946-0542;
Julie.Orr@usda.gov.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
Background
Under the Plant Protection Act (7 U.S.C. 7701et seq.), the Secretary of Agriculture is authorized to take such actions as may be necessary to prevent the introduction and spread of plant pests and noxious weeds within the United States. The Secretary has delegated this authority to the Administrator of the Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS) within the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA).
Pursuant to the regulations in 7 CFR part 319, APHIS prohibits or restricts the importation of plants and plant products into the United States to prevent the introduction of plant pests that are not already established in the United States or plant pests that may be established but are under official control.
The regulations in Subpart P—Cut Flowers, §§ 319.74-1 through 319.74-4 (referred to below as the regulations), govern the importation of cut flowers into the United States. Section 319.74-2 of the regulations contains conditions governing the importation of fresh cut flowers. Paragraph (a) provides that all imported cut flowers are subject to inspection at ports of entry into the United States, while paragraph (b) describes, in general terms, actions that APHIS may require if cut flowers are found during the inspection to be infested with a plant pest.
Paragraphs (c) and (d) of § 319.74-2 contain requirements regarding specific types of cut flowers. Paragraph (c) provides that any cut flower found upon inspection to be infested with agromyzids (leaf-miners) must be fumigated with methyl bromide in accordance with 7 CFR part 305, which contains our phytosanitary treatment regulations. Paragraph (d) lists the cut flowers of the genera
Chrysanthemum, Leucanthemella,
and
Nipponanthemum
that are considered to be hosts of chrysanthemum white rust (
Puccinia horiana
P. Henn., CWR) and countries in which CWR is known to exist. It explains that in order for any of these cut flowers to be imported into the United States, they must be grown in a place of production that is registered with the national plant protection organization (NPPO) of the respective country and that is subject to inspection by an APHIS-approved inspector; must be accompanied by a phytosanitary certification or equivalent documentation issued by the NPPO of the exporting country or their designee with an additional declaration that the place of production and the consignment itself were inspected and found free of CWR; and must have the identity of the registered production site marked on their box as well as other shipping documents that accompany the cut flowers.
On April 17, 2023, we published in the
Federal Register
a proposed rule (88 FR 23365-23368, Docket No. APHIS-2019-0024) [1]
to amend the regulations governing the importation of fresh cut flowers to remove requirements for the importation of specific types of cut flowers from the regulations, and to list them in the U.S. Department of Agriculture database called the Agricultural Commodity Import Requirements (ACIR) database instead. We also proposed a notice-based, streamlined approach to update the import requirements for fresh cut flowers.
We also proposed to remove entirely any restrictions on the importation of fresh cut flowers of the genera
Chrysanthemum, Leucanthemella,
and
Nipponanthemum
from countries in which CWR is known to exist. We proposed to relieve such restrictions based on an economic evaluation analysis, titled “Economic Evaluation of the Regulatory Policy for Chrysanthemum White Rust (CWR) (
Puccinia horiana
Henn.) in the United States,” which we made available for public comment along with the proposed rule. (The EE was initially completed in 2019; however, APHIS reviewed the document in September 2026 and confirmed that the 2019 data analyzed remains accurate.) Through the EE, APHIS determined that the United States eradication policy for CWR is no longer technically and economically justified. Specifically, APHIS found that efforts to eradicate CWR are costly because the pathogen can overwinter and survive in dormant below-ground parts, with a latency of expression. Additionally, APHIS found that fungicides are available and provide growers with a compliance alternative at a fraction of the cost of the value of a chrysanthemum plant. To that end, APHIS determined that CWR is no longer considered a pest of quarantine
( printed page 64254)
significance and should be moved to a management phase. We also proposed adding two definitions to the regulations, for “ACIR” and “quarantine pest.”
We solicited comments concerning our proposal for 60 days ending June 16, 2023.
APHIS received 21 comments by that date. They were from flower importers, exporters, distributors, breeders, shippers, flower industry trade groups, and government agencies.
Of the 21 comments received, 20 supported the rule, while one additional commenter registered no comment or concern. Several technical clarifications were requested, however. The comments received are discussed below.
A commenter requested an explanation of the differences and advantages of the notice-based process.

articles.full_text:
Palantir (PLTR +2.40%) has become one of the biggest names in artificial intelligence (AI), but the boom is still in its early innings, and there's plenty of time for new leaders to rise. Over the next five years, the biggest winners may be the companies quietly building the infrastructure that makes the AI revolution possible. Celestica (CLS -4.05%) and Marvell Technology (MRVL -3.52%) fit that description, thanks to their cutting-edge tech.
Celestica: The AI infrastructure enabler hiding in plain sight
If the physical end of the AI boom continues to shift toward entire AI factories, Celestica could be sitting in one of the most important parts of the supply chain. That's because the company is increasingly involved in designing and manufacturing the data center infrastructure that connects AI compute.
Key Data Points
That transformation is already showing up in the business. In the second quarter, Celestica's revenue jumped 62% year over year, and management raised its full-year outlook. It also said it expects its growth to accelerate in 2027, and that adjusted earnings growth would outpace revenue growth. Management pointed to new program wins and improving customer forecasts as drivers of that upbeat guidance.
Plus, it's not just about selling more servers. Celestica is moving deeper into advanced AI systems. For example, the company announced a collaboration with AMD to bring the Helios rack-scale AI platform to market, with Celestica responsible for the research and development (R&D), design, and manufacturing of scale-up networking switches that connect clusters of AMD's AI accelerators.
That matters because AI infrastructure is becoming even more complex. As successive generations of processors increase their compute power, the challenge becomes more about moving data between accelerators, memory, and different parts of the data center. Celestica can help solve those connectivity issues and benefit no matter what type of AI chips a data center operator is using.
Celestica is also attracting attention because of its relationships with major AI players. For example, the company has worked with Google on its custom processors and with OpenAI on its next-generation AI systems.
Marvell, on the other hand, is tackling the same opportunity from a different angle: designing custom chips tailored to specific AI workloads.
Marvell: Betting on the custom AI chip revolution
Marvell has made a name for itself as one of the biggest suppliers to AI giants, especially as hyperscalers look beyond off-the-shelf chips to more customized AI infrastructure. In just a few years, its custom silicon business has grown from essentially nothing to roughly a quarter of its data center revenue, while its optical interconnect segment has grown rapidly as AI systems require more bandwidth.
Key Data Points
Meanwhile, management said that its AI-related bookings were exceptionally strong and that demand was broad across high-speed optics, Ethernet switching, and data center interconnect. That means Marvell isn't betting on the success of a single software platform like Palantir, but is benefiting from several layers of the physical AI build-out, including accelerators and memory interfaces, networking, optical connectivity, and advanced packaging.
It even expanded its relationship with Google, extending its commercial agreement to cover custom silicon integrated into Google's Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) ecosystem, including AI inference chips, storage controllers, and near-memory compute.
Then there's its relationship with Nvidia. Marvell Technology and Nvidia announced a partnership around NVLink Fusion, giving customers building on Nvidia's infrastructure access to Marvell's custom chips and scale-up networking. As a sweetener, Nvidia invested $2 billion in Marvell, too.
If AI infrastructure continues to become more customized, Marvell could be one of the biggest winners in the next phase of the AI race.
Why Celestica and Marvell could outshine Palantir in five years
Market cap tells the real story here. Palantir sits at around $462 billion today, Marvell at about $252 billion, and Celestica at about $45 billion. That means Marvell would need to almost double its market cap to catch up to the data analytics giant, while Celestica would need roughly tenfold growth, a much taller order by any means.
Let's assume Palantir's earnings multiple keeps compressing toward 20, roughly where its own forward estimates already point. Its earnings growth would largely offset that compression, leaving its market cap near $460 billion, where it sits today, rather than pushing it higher.
For Marvell, EPS is projected to climb more than sixfold from $4.22 in its fiscal 2027, which just began, to $27.77 by its fiscal 2031. That means even with a modest rerating downward, let alone a flat earnings multiple, the stock could more than double based on earnings growth alone.
But for Celestica, a lot more would need to go right. Consensus EPS estimates climb from $11.21 this year to north of $41 by 2030, but for the stock to 10x, its growth would have to keep compounding, and the stock's P/E multiple would have to expand rather than contract the way a static forward table implies.
Marvell's growth trajectory could easily turn it into a larger company than Palantir in five years. Celestica can reach that size too, but it will need both its earnings growth and its P/E multiple to break in its favor.

articles.summary: Oil prices jump on tanker attacks and slowing flows through Strait of Hormuz  Financial TimesOil prices jump as Iran steps up tanker attacks, hurricane threatens U.S. Gulf production  CNBCOil prices jump amid record tanker attacks in Hormuz  CNNOil rises 4% on revived Middle East worries, Hurricane Isaias supply disruption  ReutersOil prices climb above $105 as bond yields rise  Yahoo Finance
articles.full_text:
Simply sign up to the Oil myFT Digest -- delivered directly to your inbox.
Oil prices surged as much as 5 per cent on Thursday, pushing Brent above $105 a barrel, following an escalation of hostilities in the Middle East and amid signs that a revival in shipping through the Strait of Hormuz is petering out.
The international crude benchmark climbed sharply after tankers were hit by missiles in the Gulf and off the coast of Oman late on Wednesday, and Saudi Arabia said three people were killed in Houthi attacks on its airports this week. It later fell back and settled 4.1 per cent higher at $104.28.
Oil prices had eased in the second half of September as shipping picked up through the strait, a vital channel connecting Middle Eastern oil producers with international markets.
But traffic has dipped again following an increase in hostilities this month, including a strike on a tanker off Qatar on Wednesday evening.
Data from trade consultancy Kpler showed that average weekly flows through the Strait of Hormuz climbed as high as 15mn barrels a day in late September, almost 90 per cent of prewar levels.
But these have since fallen back to about 11mn b/d. Preliminary data showed just 4mn barrels transiting the strait on Tuesday.
“The whole story that flows through the Strait of Hormuz have returned has been turned upside down,” said Arne Lohmann Rasmussen, chief analyst at Global Risk Management.
UK Maritime Trade Operations, which monitors shipping, reported nine attacks on vessels near the strait in the first week of October, after 13 over the course of September.
It said it was advised on Wednesday evening that a tanker had been struck by multiple projectiles off the coast of Qatar and that casualties had been reported.
Separate maritime security sources said Iran had fired missiles at a tanker off the coast of Oman on Wednesday night, the first such attack outside the strait for a month.
Saudi Arabia said a man and two women were killed in separate attacks claimed by Iran-backed Houthis on two Saudi airports on Tuesday and Wednesday, with dozens of people injured.
The Atlantic magazine reported on Wednesday that US President Donald Trump was considering a plan to strike Iran before the midterm elections in November.
Brent gave up part of its earlier gains on Thursday after Trump said in a post on his Truth Social platform that the US had been having “productive discussions” with Iran and “will not be attacking” the Islamic republic before the elections.
A hurricane in the Gulf of Mexico has forced some US producers to halt production, adding to the upward pressure on prices. West Texas Intermediate, the US benchmark, settled 3.6 per cent higher at $91.49 a barrel, but had been up more than 5 earlier in the day.
Much of the oil transiting the Strait of Hormuz in recent months has done so via shuttle services in which a small number of tankers cross the waterway and transfer cargoes to ships waiting outside the Gulf.
The resulting high cost of shipping, along with a sharp reduction in refining capacity, has boosted prices of crude and of refined products.
Brent is trading about 45 per cent above its price on the eve of the Iran war, while European diesel is up almost 100 per cent.
Additional reporting by Alice Hancock and Ian Smith in London

AGENCY:
Enforcement and Compliance, International Trade Administration, Department of Commerce.
SUMMARY:
The U.S. Department of Commerce (Commerce) determines that chromium trioxide from India is being, or is likely to be, sold in the United States at less than fair value (LTFV). The period of investigation (POI) is July 1, 2024, through June 30, 2025.
DATES:
Applicable October 8, 2026.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
Katerina Katsiadas, AD/CVD Operations, Office VIII, Enforcement and Compliance, International Trade Administration, U.S. Department of Commerce, 1401 Constitution Avenue NW, Washington, DC 20230; telephone: (202) 482-4929.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
Background
On May 22, 2026, Commerce published in the
Federal Register
its preliminary affirmative determination in the LTFV investigation of chromium trioxide from India, and invited interested parties to comment on the
Preliminary Determination.[1]
No interested parties submitted comments on the
Preliminary Determination.
Accordingly, the final determination remains unchanged from, and hereby adopts, the
Preliminary Determination,
and no decision memorandum accompanies this notice. The deadline for this final determination is October 5, 2026.[2]
Scope of the Investigation
The product covered by this investigation is chromium trioxide from India. For a complete description of the scope of this investigation,
see
the appendix to this notice.
Scope Comments
We received no comments from interested parties on the scope of the investigation as it appeared in the
Preliminary Determination.[3]
Therefore, we made no changes to the scope of the investigation.
Verification
Because the mandatory respondent in this investigation, did not provide information requested by Commerce, Commerce did not conduct a verification in this investigation.
Use of Adverse Facts Available
As discussed in the
Preliminary Determination,
Commerce assigned to mandatory respondent Vishnu Chemicals Limited (Vishnu Chemicals) an estimated weighted-average dumping margin on the basis of adverse facts available (AFA), pursuant to sections 776(a) and (b) of the Tariff Act of 1930, as amended (the Act). There is no new information, or new arguments, on the record that warrant reconsideration of the
Preliminary Determination.
Thus, we made no changes to our analysis or to the estimated weighted-average dumping margins for the final determination. For a full description of the methodology underlying Commerce's final determination,
see
the
Preliminary Determination.
All-Others Rate
Section 735(c)(5)(A) of the Act, and Commerce's regulations at 19 CFR 351.109(f)(1), provide that the estimated weighted-average dumping margin for all other producers and exporters not individually investigated shall be equal to the weighted average of the estimated weighted-average dumping margins established for exporters and producers individually investigated, excluding rates that are zero,
de minimis,
or determined entirely under section 776 of the Act.[4]
When there is no individually-calculated estimated weighted-average dumping margin that is not zero,
de minimis,
or based entirely on facts available, section 735(c)(5)(B) of the Act directs Commerce to “use any reasonable method to establish the estimated all-others rate for exporters and producers not individually investigated.” [5]
In an LTFV investigation, when the estimated-weighted-average dumping margins for all individually investigated companies are determined entirely on the basis of AFA, Commerce's practice is to calculate the all-others rate as an average of the dumping margins alleged in the petition.[6]
( printed page 64336)
In the
Preliminary Determination,
we assigned an estimated weighted-average dumping margin of 14.44 percent (
i.e.,
the sole dumping margin alleged in the petition) to all other exporters and producers, pursuant to section 735(c)(5)(B) of the Act.[7]
As noted above, we received no comments in opposition to the all-others rate established in our
Preliminary Determination,
which is derived from the only reliable information available from which to establish an all-others rate in the absence of an individually-calculated dumping margin that is not zero,
de minimis,
or based entirely on facts available. Therefore, we continue to assign an estimated weighted-average dumping margin of 14.44 percent to all other exporters and producers for this final determination.
